headline: Committee recommends agriculture grants bill, discusses Kīhei teacher housing purchase

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: Seven members voted aye on the agriculture grants bill. The committee also heard retirement system and health fund updates, and the council is set to consider the Kīhei housing agreement this Friday.
meeting.recap: The committee heard updates from the state retirement system and employee health benefits fund.[[0:08:18]] The retirement system leader said Maui County paid $5.8 million for pension spiking, or sharp pay jumps before retirement.[[0:21:48]] The health fund leader said the County is projected to fully fund retiree health costs in 2031.[[0:44:23]] Seven members voted aye to recommend the agriculture grants bill.[[2:35:07]] Wildfire survivors not eligible for FEMA help could move in within a month after the state buys it.[[2:54:54]] A council member raised concern that no permanent affordable rentals are planned for West Maui.[[3:00:47]] The environmental management director asked to file (close out) Bill 40, a budget bill for debris disposal sites.[[3:51:33]]
meeting.next: The chair asked members to forward their audit questions so they can be sent to the department. The finance department will come back with real excise tax numbers. The administration will check the property's community plan designation and report back before Friday's vote. The department will refine its debris site request and come back with a revised budget amendment.

issues.oneLine: A state-bought former hotel in Kīhei would become teacher housing, workforce rentals and public pre-kindergarten classrooms.
issues.why: The administration said the project helps meet an ongoing need for housing local workers can afford.

deadlines.t: Council vote on the bill authorizing the mayor to enter the agreement.
State closes on the property purchase.

deadlines.t: County publishes request for proposals seeking a developer.

issues.next: The council is set to consider approving the agreement this Friday.
issues.brief: Teacher households are those with a full-time pre-K, primary or secondary teacher at a public or accredited private school.[[#1]] Tenants would have to recertify their income every year.[[#2]] Units would be split into thirds for households at 80%, 100% and 120% of the area median income (the middle income for the area).[[#3]] The $45 million to buy the property is state money appropriated by the legislature.[[#4]]

issues.brief: The state plans to open the Kīhei building to wildfire survivors who are not eligible for FEMA reimbursement.[[#1]] All wildfire debris, whether owners opted in or out of the government program, will end up at the permanent site in Central Maui.[[#2]]
